thread:
maya: thinking about expanding our spot pools to a heterogenous GPU mix (A10G, L40, and a few H100 variants). what's everyone's take on bin-packing vs price-first allocation here?
alek: price-first saves $, but we've seen 2x variance in latency for some A10G-packed batches. not great for tail-SLOs.
sanjay: +1. bin-packing by memory/compute class reduces fragmentation. also needs smarter pod sizing.
maya: can we do hybrid? prefer cheaper instances but fall back to higher-perf ones when latency grows. is that doable with current autoscaler?
rachel: telemetry-wise we need per-instance token/sec and p90 latency. we don't have per-GPU breakdown in the dashboard today, only per-node. will add a graph.
toni: for fallbacks we should hook into the preemption handler. checkpoint frequency matters — if we checkpoint every 30s it's too noisy. aiming for N seconds of tolerated lost work.
alek: rough numbers from last week: A10G median cost/hr 0.8x, p95 latency +15%. L40 is 0.95x cost, p95 +5%. H100 is 2.8x cost but p95 baseline.
maya: sounds like policy: prefer A10G pool for bulk, L40 as balancing tier, H100 reserved for latency-critical routes. can we auto-route by request latency budget?
sanjay: yes — route by hint in request header (x-latency-budget: ms). the runtime can try cheaper pools first and if it predicts >budget, route to a higher tier. need a cheap predictor.
infra-bot: NOTICE: we had 3 spot preemptions in us-west-2 on 1745123800 affecting A10G pool. 12/120 nodes reclaimed. auto-scale recovered to baseline in 2m 40s.
rachel: we should test interruption scenarios end-to-end. add a chaos job that simulates 20% preemptions on the cheap pool for 1h and run smoke/eval traffic.
toni: for interruption handling, implement async checkpoint + resume via objectstore. small change: use incremental KV checkpointing to avoid full model state writes. here's a sample instance_group config we can try: 
```
instance_groups:
  - name: spot-a10g
    types: [a10g.large, a10g.xlarge, a10g.2x]
    priority: 10
    binpack_by: [gpu_mem, gpu_count]
  - name: spot-l40
    types: [l40.large, l40.xlarge]
    priority: 20
    binpack_by: [gpu_mem]
  - name: reserved-h100
    types: [h100.8xlarge]
    priority: 100
    fallback: false
```
maya: that looks good. how do we evaluate perf/price tradeoff? can we run a 24h A/B with real inference traces?
alek: yes — spin two fleets: current baseline and the mixed strategy. measure cost/token, p95 latency, and %requests hitting H100. also track evictions.
sanjay: small ops note: make sure CUDA/cuDNN versions align across instance types. we've hit silent failures when kernels differ.
rachel: i'll schedule the A/B and add dashboards for cost/token and p95 by pool. tagging @eng-sre for runbook updates.
maya: thanks all. next step: toni + sanjay to prototype autoscaler hints, alek to prepare cost model, rachel to schedule A/B. aim to start next Tue. :rocket:
